newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu, Clinton to discuss Israel-Syria talks.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu, Clinton to discuss Israel-Syria talks.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, on his second trip to the United States since June, meets President Bill Clinton on Monday to discuss ways of reviving faltering peace moves between Syria and Israel.
Netanyahu told reporters before flying to Washington that the United States and other parties were helping in efforts to resume peace talks suspended last March.
"We made various proposals on this issue which in my opinion are reasonable and logical and yes, there are contacts being held on this issue via the U.S. as well," Netanyahu said.
In five years of intermittent negotiations sponsored by the United States, Israel and Syria have failed to agree on terms for peace.
Syria wants Israel to withdraw from all of the Golan Heights, a strategic plateau the Jewish state captured in the 1967 Middle East war. Netanyahu says the Golan must remain under Israel's control.

Syria has rejected an initiative by Netanyahu, who ousted Nobel Peace Prize laureate Shimon Peres in a national election last May, to withdraw Israeli troops from Lebanon where Damascus is the main powerbroker, as a first step towards a wider peace.
Instead, Syria wants talks with Israel to pick up where they left off in March when Peres, who was ready for at least a partial withdrawal, was heading the government.

"The renewal of talks with Syria is one of the issues I will discuss in Washington but I want to emphasise that this government is not the previous government. It was elected on a different platform," Netanyahu said.
"Whoever expects that we will adopt the positions of our predecessors probably doesn't understand the democratic process in Israel," he said.
Netanyahu was also expected to brief Clinton on a meeting the Israeli leader held with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat near the Gaza Strip last week.
Palestinian and Israeli officials overseeing implementation of Israel-PLO peace deals were to meet on Monday for the first time since Netanyahu's election.
Saeb Erekat, head of the Palestinian side in the joint steering and monitoring committee, said Palestinians would focus on the issue of Hebron.

"Our priority in Monday's meeting is Hebron. We will discuss mechanisms for redeployment from Hebron after finalising protocols on deployment of temporary international presence in the city and joint patrols," Erekat told Reuters.
He said the meeting would take place at his West Bank office in PLO-ruled Jericho.

Palestinians have complained that Netanyahu's government, formed in June, is not honouring the agreements -- foremost Israel's commitment to withdraw from the West Bank town of Hebron, home to 100,000 Palestinians and around 400 Jewish settlers.
